text:
alex: Noticing a steady p99 increase for token-gen on a handful of US-WEST racks starting ~03:10 UTC. p50 steady, p99 jumped from ~2.8s -> ~4.3s. GPU util on those hosts is ~98%.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-util-high on rack-usw2-r18 (hosts 18.22.3.*). https://telemetry.internal/alerts/ALRT-6523

priya: Quick check: NIC RX errors and TCP retransmits spiked at the same time. short netstat sample: `tcp_retransmits: 1200` in a 1m window.

matt: My hunch is KV cache regen + egress saturation. When regen hits, we see PCIe stall counters and DMA bursts.

sasha: Which tenants are on those hosts? I see an RLHF tenant, a batch rerank tenant, and a low-latency chat tenant in the same slice.

alex: tenant map: tenant-a (RLHF), tenant-b (rerank batch), tenant-c (chat). tenant-a & tenant-b share slice-7823.

dana: If we carve out tenant-a to fractional dedicated we'll trigger committed capacity; need a quick cost estimate before approving.

priya: Probing hosts: `ssh rack-usw2-r18-22 'nvidia-smi dmon -s u'` shows sustained encode spikes on GPU0-3. `ethtool -S eth0` reveals rx_no_buf increments -> driver/NIC pressure.

matt: That matches previous incidents where vGPU/large-batch DMA bursts starved NIC queues. Could be IO path contention.

sasha: Remediation options (short): 1) apply per-slice egress shaping, 2) soft-preempt tenant-b batch jobs, 3) migrate tenant-a to a fractional dedicated warm slice. Preference?

alex: lean 1 then 3. Shaping is fastest. How targeted can we be?

priya: We can apply `egress_cap` per slice. Example: `POST /allocator/config {"slice_id":"slice-7823","egress_cap_mbps":350}`. Observed current egress ~900Mbps.

dana: Migration cost question: tenant-a uses ~12 GPU-hours/hr when hot. Fractional dedicated for this profile ~ $1.8/hr + warmup delta. Migration/warmup may add 5-15% token cost during handoff.

matt: I'll prepare a canary migration plan in parallel. Short plan:
```
1) mark tenant-a migrate:candidate
2) provision fractional dedicated `ded-slice-0821` with 2x burst headroom
3) warm KV by replaying last 10m of hashed prompts (rate-limited)
4) shift routing weights 10%->50%->100% over 5/10/20m windows
5) monitor p99 and rx_errs; rollback if destination p99 > +10%
```

infra-bot: NOTE: allocator-change requested by priya at 1881233384. Change queued.

sasha: Also consider NIC tuning short-term: coalescing tweaks reduced rx_no_buf in past events. Could avoid migration if shaping helps.

priya: I'm going to apply the egress cap to slice-7823 now (cap=350mbps). Propagation ~90s.

alex: go for it. @matt start the canary prep so it's ready if shaping doesn't stabilize. Post steps here so on-call SRE can follow.

matt: Starting canary provisioning now. Creating `ded-slice-0821`. Kicking warmup jobs. ETA first 10% traffic shift 10m.

sasha: Reminder: if KV warmup is slow we can replay hashed prompts only to avoid cold misses. Cold-start QoS hit is worse than a short warmup cost.

priya: After applying cap, telemetry shows RX errors dropping on hosts 18.22.3.*. p99 trending down to ~3.2s after ~3m. PCIe stall counters also reduced.

dana: Cost policy: if we keep a dedicated carveout >6h we'll need pre-approval from infra finance. For now, shaping + soft-preempt is cheaper.

alex: OK team, monitor for 30m. If p99 < 3.0s and RX errors stay low we avoid carveout. If not, proceed with migration and loop in product for cost tradeoffs.

matt: I'll draft a short runbook with lessons and a new pre-check (egress pressure check before warm-pool placements). Will paste link soon.

sasha: Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: RESOLVED: ALRT-6523 closed at 1881234899 (p99 recovered).
